title: The characteristic subgroup growth of a free group of rank $r\geq 2$ is of type $n^{\mathrm{log}(n)}$
author: Liam Hanany and Alexander Lubotzky
difficulty_reason: Counted unit: original Theorem 1.1 of the article (source label Characteristic Growth of Free Groups, source0.tex lines 65--68), that for every $r\geq 2$ the characteristic subgroup growth of the free group $F_r$ has type $n^{\mathrm{log}(n)}$, delivered with the author's own complete 9-line proof at source0.tex lines 154--162. H2: although short, the proof is the endpoint of a research-level chain that the solver must assemble from the delivered context. It must recognise the Zassenhaus filtration $D_n$ as a descending characteristic filtration, use the automorphism-action lemma to see that the $\mathrm{Aut}(F_r)$-action on every subquotient $D_n/D_{n+1}$ factors through the fixed finite group $\mathrm{SL}^{\pm1}_r(\mathbb{F}_p)$ acting on $D_1/D_2$, convert the dimension estimate of Corollary 2.7 into a lower bound $\dim(D_n/D_{n+1})\geq\frac{1}{15}\log_p N$ for $N=[G:D_{n+1}]$, count the $\mathrm{SL}^{\pm1}_r(\mathbb{F}_p)$-submodules of that section by Corollary 2.5, lift each submodule to a characteristic subgroup of index at most $N$, and thereby produce $e^{\Omega_{p,r}(\log(n)^2)}$ characteristic subgroups of index at most $n$. That passage from a filtration of a free group to a sharp count of characteristic subgroups is well beyond ordinary PhD qualifying level.
